channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Uzbekistan Airports Reduce Tariffs for Handling Imported Livestock
item.description: Uzbekistan has introduced reduced tariffs at international airports for handling imported livestock. Uzbekistan Airports company offers special preferential rates for processing cattle, sheep, and goats arriving by air. These new conditions aim to lower costs for entrepreneurs importing agricultural animals, making air transport more accessible. The measures cover key operations like unloading and temporary storage.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's gold exports plummet, imports surge in first half of 2026
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's precious metal trade saw a significant imbalance in January-June 2026, with imports exceeding exports by 93 times. Exports totaled $680,600, while imports reached $63.6 million, primarily driven by raw gold from Kazakhstan. The country has become a net importer of precious metals and jewelry.

item.title: Former MP Tokon Mamytov Denies Signing 'Letter of 75'
item.description: Former member of parliament Tokon Mamytov denied signing the 'Letter of 75' during court proceedings in Bishkek. The letter, signed by 75 individuals including former officials and cultural figures, urged President Sadyr Japarov to schedule presidential elections for 2026 instead of January 2027. Mamytov stated he did not sign the document.

item.title: Eurasia Organization to Open Yurt at World Nomad Games Ethno-Village
item.description: The Eurasia autonomous non-commercial organization is an official partner of the VI World Nomad Games. Within the ethno-village in Kyrchyn Gorge, Eurasia will host a yurt offering interactive programs for visitors. The yurt will feature national games, presentations, master classes, and cultural dialogues. The World Nomad Games will take place in Kyrgyzstan from August 31 to September 6.

item.title: Nurbek Bukuev Appointed Deputy Minister of Health in Kyrgyzstan
item.description: Nurbek Bukuev has been appointed Deputy Minister of Health of Kyrgyzstan, replacing Bakytbek Kadyraliev. Bukuev, who has headed the National Center of Oncology and Hematology since 2024, is a surgeon, oncologist, and doctor of medical sciences with 21 years of experience. He also holds the title of «Excellent Healthcare Worker of the Kyrgyz Republic.»

item.title: Head of Kyrgyzstan's Oncology Center appointed Deputy Minister of Health
item.description: Nurbek Bukuev, formerly the head of the National Center for Oncology and Hematology in Bishkek, has been appointed Deputy Minister of Health of Kyrgyzstan. He replaces Bakytbek Kadyraliev. Bukuev is a surgeon, oncologist-gynecologist, and doctor of medical sciences with 21 years of experience.

item.title: Saida Mirziyoyeva discusses railway, governance, and economic cooperation with China's Wang Yi
item.description: Saida Mirziyoyeva, head of the Presidential Administration, met with Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi in Beijing. They discussed Uzbekistan's interest in learning from China's governance experience, particularly in poverty reduction, and deepening cooperation in agriculture, science, education, and the digital economy. The China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan railway project was also discussed.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan to Host Sixth World Nomad Games in 2026
item.description: Kyrgyzstan will host the Sixth World Nomad Games from August 31 to September 6, 2026, expecting guests from over one hundred countries. The games will combine ethnosport, ethno-culture, traditional knowledge, and scientific/educational programs. The concept emphasizes the inseparable link between nomadic games and the history and lifestyle of the peoples who created them.

item.title: Women's Crime in Kyrgyzstan Rises 22 Percent Year-to-Date
item.description: From January to July 2026, Kyrgyzstan identified 13,490 offenders, an 11.4 percent increase from the previous year. The number of female offenders rose by 22 percent to 1,899, constituting 14.1 percent of the total. Male offenders increased by 9.8 percent to 11,591. Offenders aged 29 and older formed the largest group, while those aged 18-24 saw a 31.7 percent increase.

item.title: Tashkent to Launch $288 Million DP World Logistics Hub in October
item.description: Tashkent plans to attract $9 billion in investments by the end of 2026, according to Mayor Shavkat Umurzakov. A key project is the DP World logistics hub, with construction set to begin in October. The hub will be designed to handle 120 million tons of cargo and 150,000 containers. Tashkent was ranked third among the world's fastest-growing cities by Boston Consulting Group.

item.title: Astana Court Hears Testimony on Paramedic's Death, Possibility of Faster Response
item.description: The Inter-District Criminal Court in Astana continued the trial regarding the death of paramedic Uldana Myrzuan. A senior paramedic from the medical team present on the day of the incident testified, along with the head of the emergency department. The prosecution requested to question another paramedic, Aktymak Sizdykova, who reportedly provided assistance to the deceased. The defense objected, but the judge granted the request.

item.title: Former Kyrgyz Ombudsman Denies Signing 'Letter 75' in Court
item.description: Former Kyrgyz Ombudsman Tokon Mamytov stated in Bishkek City Court that he did not sign the 'Letter 75' appeal. The case concerns the alleged preparation for a violent seizure of power. Mamytov was listed as a signatory but testified he did not put his signature on the document. The appeal, published in February 2026, proposed early presidential elections to President Sadyr Japarov and then-Speaker Nurlanbek Turgunbek uulu.

item.title: Female crime in Kyrgyzstan increased by 22 percent since the beginning of the year
item.description: In January-July 2026, law enforcement agencies in Kyrgyzstan identified 13,490 offenders, an 11.4 percent increase from the previous year. Female crime saw a significant rise of 22 percent, reaching 1,899 individuals, which constitutes 14.1 percent of the total. Male crime increased by 9.8 percent.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan aims to restore 300,000 hectares of degraded land by 2030
item.description: Central Asia faces significant land degradation, with over 80 million hectares affected, impacting millions of people and causing annual economic losses of $2-6 billion. Climate change exacerbates the issue, leading to increased sandstorms and threats to water resources. Kyrgyzstan plans to restore 300,000 hectares of degraded land by 2030.

item.title: Kazakhstan Considers Banning Social Media Access for Under-16s
item.description: Kazakhstan is considering a ban on social media registration for individuals under 16 years old. The draft law, developed by the government, has been submitted to parliament. President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev also instructed the cabinet to strengthen content filtering for children and expand the use of special children's SIM cards.

item.title: Wall Painting from 4th-5th Century Discovered at Boburtepa Archaeological Site
item.description: Archaeological excavations at the Boburtepa site in Uzbekistan's Qashqadaryo region have uncovered remnants of an ancient building and a unique wall painting. The artwork, depicting tulips and white flowers with red wavy lines, was found on a western wall and dates back to the 4th-5th centuries AD. Experts suggest the structure may have been a temple.

item.title: Suspects Detained for Brutal Attack on Woman in Turkistan Region
item.description: Two men have been detained in connection with a brutal attack on a woman in the Turkistan region of Kazakhstan. The suspects allegedly broke into the woman's home, assaulted her, and stole her mobile phone. A criminal case has been initiated, and police are investigating the circumstances of the incident.

item.title: Osh construction company fined 200,000 soms for safety violations
item.description: A company in Osh, 'Naiman Iygiilik,' was fined 200,000 soms for violations at a construction site for a 12-story building. Inspectors found the excavation extended beyond the site's boundaries, posing a danger to passersby. The company was ordered to fix the issue and improve safety measures.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's non-tax budget revenues significantly increased in 2025
item.description: Non-tax revenues in Kyrgyzstan grew by 88 billion soms to 189.5 billion soms in 2025, according to the Ministry of Finance. This increased their share of GDP from 6.4% to 9.6%. Key sources include state share dividends, National Bank profits, and paid government services.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Aims to Restore 300,000 Hectares of Degraded Land by 2030
item.description: Central Asia faces significant land degradation, with over 80 million hectares affected, impacting agriculture and livelihoods. Climate change exacerbates the issue, causing faster warming and glacier melt. Dust storms, fueled by drought and heat, spread pollutants and harm crops, transport, and health. Kyrgyzstan plans to restore 300,000 hectares of degraded land by 2030.

item.title: Kyrgyzfarmatsiya to Directly Purchase Spinal Implants from Turkish Manufacturer
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's state enterprise Kyrgyzfarmatsiya has signed a memorandum of understanding with Turkish company Mikron Medical. The agreement aims to facilitate direct cooperation for supplying orthopedic and spinal implants to Kyrgyz medical institutions. This direct partnership is expected to reduce intermediaries and potentially lower procurement costs for medical devices.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's state budget revenue projected to reach 1.15 trillion soms by 2031
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's state budget revenues are projected to reach 791.1 billion soms in 2027 and 1,148.6 trillion soms by 2031, according to the Ministry of Finance. The ministry forecasts budget revenues to be 28.9 percent of GDP in 2027, declining to 23.1 percent by 2031. Expenditures are expected to rise from 758.7 billion soms in 2027 to 1,049.4 trillion soms in 2031. The ministry plans to maintain a budget surplus, with funds allocated for economic development and public debt repayment.

item.title: Kyrgyz citizens can still enter Kazakhstan without prior authorization
item.description: Kazakhstan has introduced new digital migration mechanisms, including the QazETA pre-entry approval system. However, Kyrgyzstan's Foreign Ministry clarified that citizens of Kyrgyzstan do not currently need prior authorization to travel to Kazakhstan. A Kyrgyz MP met with the Kyrgyz Consul General in Almaty to discuss the new rules and the protection of Kyrgyz citizens' rights.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's non-tax budget revenues are increasing significantly
item.description: Non-tax revenues in Kyrgyzstan's budget are on the rise, projected to reach 189.5 billion soms in 2025, an increase of 88 billion soms. The share of non-tax revenues in GDP grew from 6.4% to 9.6% within a year. Key sources include dividends from state-owned companies, National Bank profits, fees, and other non-tax receipts. Projections estimate non-tax revenues at 149.2 billion soms in 2027 and 189.9 billion soms by 2031.

item.title: North Kazakhstan resident jailed for illegal lending, assets seized
item.description: A resident of North Kazakhstan has been convicted for operating an illegal lending scheme without a license, earning 774 million tenge. The court has seized six apartments acquired through these illicit activities. The man was found guilty of 78 counts of illegal lending, where he provided loans to individuals unable to obtain them from banks, often masking the transactions as property sales. The verdict is not yet final.

item.title: US Kok-Boru Team Honors First Coach in Kyrgyzstan
item.description: The U.S. Kok-Boru team, led by captain Ladd Howell, visited the home of their first coach, Mirlan Srazhdinov, to honor his memory. The team presented commemorative gifts to the family and fondly recalled their mentor, who facilitated connections between American and Kyrgyz players. Srazhdinov was a player and captain for the 'Börülü' team and represented Kyrgyzstan at the first World Nomad Games.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Non-Tax Budget Revenues Show Significant Growth
item.description: Non-tax revenues in Kyrgyzstan's budget have increased significantly, reaching 189.5 billion soms in 2025, an 88 billion som rise from the previous year. This growth raised the share of non-tax revenues in GDP from 6.4% to 9.6%. Key sources include dividends from state shares, National Bank profits, state service fees, and other non-tax collections. Projections estimate non-tax revenues at 149.2 billion soms in 2027 and 189.9 billion by 2031.

item.title: Kazakh President Proposes Ban on Under-16s Using Social Media
item.description: Kazakhstan is considering a ban on social media registration for individuals under 16, with a draft law submitted to parliament. President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev emphasized the need to protect children from the influence of social media, digital platforms, and AI, citing similar measures in other countries. He also called for enhanced content filtering and the expansion of dedicated children's SIM cards to ensure 'information immunity'.

item.title: Bishkek section of Chui Avenue to close for World Nomad Games and SCO summit
item.description: A section of Chui Avenue in Bishkek will be closed to traffic from August 27 to August 29. The closure is due to security measures for the upcoming 6th World Nomad Games and the SCO summit. Drivers are advised to plan alternative routes. The SCO summit is scheduled for August 31 and September 1, with the World Nomad Games running from August 31 to September 6.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan to acquire 9 hectares of land in China's Xi'an for transport center
item.description: Kyrgyzstan plans to build a transport and logistics center in Xi'an, China, acquiring a 9-hectare plot of land. The center will be part of the Xi'an—Kashgar—Osh multimodal route, facilitating cargo transport by rail and road. This initiative aims to launch new routes and increase freight volumes before the China—Kyrgyzstan—Uzbekistan railway becomes operational.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's State Budget Revenue Expected to Reach 1.15 Trillion Som by 2031
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's state budget revenues are projected to reach 791.1 billion som in 2027 and are planned to increase to 1 trillion 148.6 billion som by 2031, according to the Ministry of Finance's fiscal and investment policy report. The ministry forecasts that budget revenues will decrease as a percentage of GDP from 28.9% in 2027 to 23.1% in 2031. State budget expenditures are expected to rise from 758.7 billion som in 2027 to 1 trillion 49.4 billion som in 2031.

item.title: Kyrgyzpharmatsiya Plans Direct Procurement of Spinal Implants from Turkish Company
item.description: State Enterprise 'Kyrgyzpharmatsiya' and Turkish company Mikron Medical have signed a memorandum of understanding to cooperate in supplying orthopedic and spinal implants to Kyrgyzstan's medical institutions. Kyrgyzpharmatsiya believes direct cooperation with manufacturers will reduce intermediaries and potentially lower procurement costs. The Turkish company's products are being considered for centralized medical device procurement in 2027.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's state budget revenue projected to reach 1.15 trillion soms by 2031
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Finance forecasts state budget revenues to reach 791.1 billion soms in 2027 and increase to 1.1486 trillion soms by 2031. The budget's share of GDP is expected to decrease from 28.9% in 2027 to 23.1% in 2031. Expenditures are projected to rise from 758.7 billion soms in 2027 to 1.0494 trillion soms in 2031.

item.title: CIA Director reportedly visited Moscow to warn against attacking NATO
item.description: The Director of the CIA reportedly made an unannounced visit to Moscow to warn Russia against attacking NATO member states, particularly Estonia, Latvia, and Lithuania. This warning comes amid concerns that Russia might test the alliance's strength. Neither Washington nor Moscow officially announced the visit or its agenda.

item.title: New Kazakhstan Entry Rules: Kyrgyz Citizens Can Still Travel Freely
item.description: Kazakhstan is implementing new digital migration mechanisms, including a preliminary entry approval system (QazETA) and a unified information database. While the Ministry of Internal Affairs plans a phased rollout from August to December 2026, potentially with service fees, Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs clarified that Kyrgyz citizens currently do not require preliminary approval for travel to Kazakhstan. Discussions are underway to analyze EAEU agreements.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Changes Family Assistance Benefit Rules Effective September 1
item.description: Kyrgyzstan will modify the criteria for granting the 'family assistance' benefit to low-income families with children under 16, effective September 1. The minimum guaranteed income will increase from 1,000 to 1,500 som. Families with cars older than 15 years will be eligible, while those owning two or more residences will be excluded. Norms for calculating income from land shares will also be updated.

item.title: Kazakhstan Considers VAT Exemption for QR Payments and Phone Transfers
item.description: Kazakhstan's financial regulators are proposing to extend the existing VAT exemption for payment card operations to cover QR code payments and phone number transfers. This move aims to create equal conditions for various cashless payment methods as digital options gain popularity. The Ministry of National Economy is involved in the discussion, with further analysis by the Ministry of Finance, the Agency for Regulation and Development of the Financial Market, and the National Bank.

item.title: Uzbekistan Discussed as Responsible Middle Power at ISMI Seminar
item.description: The Institute for Strategic and Regional Studies (ISMI) hosted a seminar on "Uzbekistan as a Responsible Middle Power," marking the country's 35th independence anniversary. The event focused on a new analytical report detailing Uzbekistan's foreign policy evolution and changes over the years, particularly in the last decade. Participants included government officials and academics.

item.title: Memorandum Signed to Study Renewable Energy Projects in Uzbekistan
item.description: Saudi company ACWA Power and South Korean Korea Western Power Co., Ltd. (KOWEPO) signed a memorandum in Tashkent to explore renewable energy opportunities in Uzbekistan. The agreement aims to jointly assess prospects for renewable energy projects, energy storage systems, and related infrastructure, potentially attracting South Korean investment.

item.title: Azerbaijan and Uzbekistan Share Common Regional Strategic Interests, Official States
item.description: Azerbaijan and Uzbekistan are united by common regional strategic interests, according to Azerbaijani Member of Parliament Shakhin Seidzade. He stated that the recent state visit of Azerbaijan's President Ilham Aliyev to Tashkent signifies a new stage in bilateral relations, moving beyond traditional cooperation to become a key component of broader regional processes.
